rounds.startFlavorText: What separates humanity from God.
rounds.endFlavorText: How the wages of sin leave a life.
rounds.teachingNote: Romans 6:23 explains why sin is serious: its wages are death, while God's gift is eternal life through Christ.

rounds.startFlavorText: One of the animals Noah gathered two by two.
rounds.endFlavorText: Another animal Noah gathered two by two.
rounds.teachingNote: Genesis 7:8-9 says animals entered the ark by pairs; this ladder uses familiar animals as a wordplay reminder of that detail.

rounds.startFlavorText: Neither cold nor this, as Revelation warns.
rounds.endFlavorText: What the covenant given at Sinai came to be called.
rounds.teachingNote: Revelation rebukes lukewarm faith as neither cold nor hot, while Hebrews contrasts the old covenant with the new.

rounds.startFlavorText: What Moses received on Mount Sinai.
rounds.endFlavorText: What the law reveals in every heart.
rounds.teachingNote: Exodus 20 gives the commandments, and Romans 7:7 says the law exposes sin by showing what God forbids.

rounds.startFlavorText: One of the three things that abide, per 1 Corinthians 13.
rounds.endFlavorText: The greatest of the three that abide.
rounds.teachingNote: 1 Corinthians 13:13 names faith, hope, and love as abiding virtues, then says love is the greatest.

rounds.startFlavorText: What the wise man built his house upon.
rounds.endFlavorText: What the foolish man built his house upon.
rounds.teachingNote: Jesus contrasts the wise builder on rock with the foolish builder on sand to picture hearing and doing His words.

rounds.startFlavorText: Neither this nor hot, as Revelation warns.
rounds.endFlavorText: A comfort promised to those who trust God.
rounds.teachingNote: Revelation uses cold and hot to expose lukewarm faith; the word warm is only a loose comfort image, not the main biblical point.

rounds.startFlavorText: What Solomon asked God to make him.
rounds.endFlavorText: A fruit of the Spirit, per Galatians 5.
rounds.teachingNote: Solomon asked for an understanding heart, and Galatians 5:22 lists kindness among the Spirit's fruit.

rounds.startFlavorText: What Jesus said is more blessed than receiving.
rounds.endFlavorText: What the thief on the cross had done in his life.
rounds.teachingNote: Acts preserves Jesus's saying that giving is more blessed, while the repentant criminal admits he deserved his punishment.
